content: Offline fallback silent degradation risks in AI-narrated reporting: (1) Graceful degradation and silent correctness failure look identical on a dashboard tracking only uptime and latency — the key question is: can the system be wrong in a way that looks fine? (2) If users receive rule-based results instead of AI results without being told, trust collapses when they discover it. (3) Production best practice: always surface to user what source/mode the narrative came from (LLM vs rule-based fallback vs empty) via an explicit source field or footer. (4) Circuit breaker pattern: monitor fallback rate; if AI is unavailable >N% of calls, alert instead of silently degrading. (5) In R packages: the report section header should differ between AI-grounded and rule-based narrative ('AI Interpretation' vs 'Methodology Summary'); the Advice field and  flag exist exactly for this. (6) Silent degradation anti-pattern: accepting empty Advice objects and rendering them without any user-visible distinction.
